sample_unit: SQL generation attempts (19 trials x 8 LLMs x 5 prompting strategies)

links.outcome: Concept mapping accuracy of GPT-4 versus USAGI baseline on 357 clinical terms
links.effect: GPT-4 achieved 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001); llama3:8b had higher effective SQL rate (75.8%) than GPT-4 (45.3%).
links.quote: GPT-4 achieved a 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001), with domain-specific performance ranging from 72.7% (drug) to 38.3% (measurement).

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM-generated queries with reference concept sets in local OMOP CDM database
links.effect: Mixed: T1D Jaccard=0.81, pregnancy 0.00, T2D 0.03, uncontrolled hypertension 0.18.
links.quote: Clinical validation revealed mixed performance: high concordance for type 1 diabetes (Jaccard=0.81), complete failure for pregnancy (Jaccard=0.00), and minimal overlap for type 2 diabetes (Jaccard=0.03), despite perfect overlap coefficients in both diabetes cases.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate in LLM-generated SQL queries
links.effect: Overall hallucination rate 32.7%; wrong domain assignments 34.2% and placeholder insertions 28.7% most common; GPT-4 33.7% vs llama3:8b 21.1%.
links.quote: The overall hallucination rate was 32.7%, with wrong domain assignments (34.2%) and placeholder insertions (28.7%) being the most common.

unlisted_practices: Three-stage preprocessing pipeline (segmentation, filtering, simplification) to reduce tokens in LLM inputs
Hybrid LLM plus rule-based approaches for complex clinical concepts

screen.reason: Empirically tests and evaluates multiple LLMs and prompting strategies for translating trial criteria into OMOP SQL queries, specifically quantifying hallucination rates and mapping performance on synthetic and retrospective institutional EHR data.

primary.practice: prompting strategies and preprocessing pipeline for hallucination reduction
